posts.title: Erasmus+ programme 2028–2034
posts.label: 🗳️ Lead committee adopted its report
posts.summary: The proposal aims to establish an education and training exchange programme for the period 2028–2034 that would allow students, trainees, and staff to study and work across participating countries. It seeks to promote cooperation between educational institutions and support skill development through mobility and learning opportunities.
posts.whatsNext: A negotiating mandate for talks with the Council would usually follow, or the report goes straight to a plenary vote. No deadline applies.

posts.title: Common system for the return of third-country nationals staying illegally in the Union (Return Regulation)
posts.label: 📜 Published in the Official Journal
posts.summary: The law establishes a unified framework for returning non-citizens who are staying illegally in the EU back to their home countries. It sets out the procedures and rules that EU countries must follow when removing undocumented migrants from their territory.
posts.whatsNext: It's law. Watch the date(s) of application — often later than entry into force, and sometimes staggered across provisions.

posts.title: Proposal for a REGULATION OF THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT AND OF THE COUNCIL amending Regulation (EU) 2024/1787 on the reduction of methane emissions in the energy sector as regards the postponement of certain obligations
posts.label: 📋 New legislative proposal
posts.summary: This proposal would delay certain requirements that energy companies must follow to reduce methane gas leaks from their operations. The postponement would apply to specific obligations that were set out in recently established rules on cutting methane emissions from the energy sector.
posts.whatsNext: Parliament's lead committee and the Council's working party examine it in parallel. No deadline applies at this stage; most files take one to two-plus years.

posts.title: Association of the overseas countries and territories with the EU including EU/Greenland/Denmark relations
posts.label: 🗳️ Lead committee adopted its report
posts.summary: This proposal aims to establish or adjust the framework for how overseas territories associated with European countries would relate to the EU. It also seeks to address the specific relationship between the EU and Greenland, including Denmark's role in those relations.
posts.whatsNext: Plenary vote on Parliament's (non-binding) opinion is next.

posts.title: General Fisheries Commission for the Mediterranean (GFCM): fishing in the GFCM Agreement area
posts.label: ✅ Adopted — Council gave the final green light
posts.summary: This law regulates fishing activities in the Mediterranean Sea under an international fisheries management framework. It establishes rules for fishing operations in the designated GFCM agreement area to ensure sustainable management of fish stocks.
posts.whatsNext: Signature by the Parliament and Council presidents, then publication in the Official Journal. It enters into force on the date the act sets — by default the 20th day after publication.

posts.title: Programme for agile and rapid defence innovation (AGILE)
posts.label: ✅ Adopted — Council gave the final green light
posts.summary: This programme supports faster development and testing of new defence technologies and military innovations. It helps defence companies and researchers bring new ideas to market more quickly through streamlined processes.
posts.whatsNext: Signature by the Parliament and Council presidents, then publication in the Official Journal. It enters into force on the date the act sets — by default the 20th day after publication.

posts.title: Banks and financial markets: settlement finality in payment and securities settlement systems
posts.label: 🧭 Council agreed its general approach
posts.summary: This proposal aims to clarify the legal rules for when payments and securities trades are considered finally settled between banks and financial institutions. It seeks to protect these settlement systems from disruption and ensure that once a transaction is confirmed, it cannot be reversed or challenged.
posts.whatsNext: The Council is ready to negotiate. Trilogue talks can start once Parliament has its mandate; where positions differ, expect negotiation.

posts.title: Amending certain Directives as regards the further development of capital market integration and supervision within the Union
posts.label: 🧭 Council agreed its general approach
posts.summary: This proposal seeks to update existing rules governing financial markets and their oversight to strengthen how capital markets operate across the EU and improve cross-border supervision. It aims to create more integrated and better-regulated financial markets throughout the union.
posts.whatsNext: The Council is ready to negotiate. Trilogue talks can start once Parliament has its mandate; where positions differ, expect negotiation.

posts.title: Amending certain Regulations as regards the further development of capital market integration and supervision within the Union
posts.label: 🧭 Council agreed its general approach
posts.summary: This proposal aims to update rules governing financial markets to help integrate them more closely across the EU and strengthen how they are overseen. The changes would seek to improve how capital markets operate and are regulated at the EU level.
posts.whatsNext: The Council is ready to negotiate. Trilogue talks can start once Parliament has its mandate; where positions differ, expect negotiation.

posts.title: Consular protection for unrepresented citizens of the Union in third countries
posts.label: 🗳️ Parliament adopted its opinion (consultation)
posts.summary: This proposal aims to allow citizens whose own country cannot help them while abroad to seek assistance from other countries in the EU instead. It seeks to ensure that no EU citizen is left without consular support when they need it in non-EU countries.
posts.whatsNext: Now in the Council's hands: it can adopt the act (usually by unanimity), amend it, or park it indefinitely — consultation sets no deadline.

posts.title: Geographical indications: aligning EU rules with changes to the provisions under the Lisbon Agreement
posts.label: 🤝 Lead committee approved the trilogue deal
posts.summary: This proposal aims to update European rules about geographical indications—special labels that protect products named after their region of origin—to match changes made to an international agreement on the same subject. The changes would ensure that European protections for regional products like Champagne or Parmigiano-Reggiano stay aligned with evolving international standards.
posts.whatsNext: The deal is provisional: it still needs a plenary vote in Parliament and formal adoption by the Council. Although confirmation is expected, either institution can still decline.

posts.title: CO2 emission class of heavy-duty vehicles with trailers
posts.label: 🗳️ Parliament adopted its 1st-reading position
posts.summary: This proposal would establish a way to classify and measure carbon dioxide emissions from large trucks when they are pulling trailers. It aims to help reduce pollution from heavy vehicles used in transport and freight.
posts.whatsNext: Council formal adoption is next, often without debate.

posts.title: Empowering France to accede to the Inter-American Convention for the Protection and Conservation of Sea Turtles
posts.label: 🗳️ Parliament adopted its 1st-reading position
posts.summary: This proposal would allow France to join an international agreement focused on protecting and conserving sea turtles in the Americas. The measure aims to extend France's commitment to safeguarding these endangered marine animals through cooperation with other countries in the region.
posts.whatsNext: Council formal adoption is next, often without debate.

posts.title: Amendments to the Critical Raw Materials Act
posts.label: 🗳️ Lead committee adopted its report
posts.summary: This proposal aims to update rules governing access to and use of materials considered essential for Europe's economy and security. The changes would likely adjust how these critical materials are sourced, processed, or managed to address new challenges or gaps in the existing framework.
posts.whatsNext: A negotiating mandate for talks with the Council would usually follow, or the report goes straight to a plenary vote. No deadline applies.

posts.whatsNext: Publication in the Official Journal is next; the act enters into force on the date it specifies (default: the 20th day after publication).

posts.title: Social security coordination
posts.label: ✍️ Signed by the European Parliament and the Council
posts.summary: This legislation coordinates social security systems across member states, ensuring that people who move between countries maintain their social security rights and benefits. It establishes rules for how social security contributions are credited and how benefits are calculated when individuals work or reside in multiple countries.
posts.whatsNext: Publication in the Official Journal is next; the act enters into force on the date it specifies (default: the 20th day after publication).

posts.summary: The law establishes a unified framework for returning non-citizens who are staying illegally in the EU back to their home countries. It sets out the procedures and rules that EU countries must follow when removing undocumented migrants from their territory.
posts.whatsNext: Publication in the Official Journal is next; the act enters into force on the date it specifies (default: the 20th day after publication).

posts.title: Sustainability-related disclosures in the financial services sector (SFDR) and key information documents for packaged retail and insurance-based investment products (PRIIPs)
posts.label: 🧭 Negotiating mandate for trilogue talks
posts.summary: The proposal aims to require financial services companies to provide clearer information about how they consider environmental and social factors in their investments. It would also standardize the way investment products are explained to consumers so they can more easily compare different options.
posts.whatsNext: Trilogue talks with the Council can begin once the Council side has its own mandate. Closed-door rounds follow; timing is not published.

posts.title: Establishment of European Business Wallets
posts.label: 🧭 Negotiating mandate for trilogue talks
posts.summary: This proposal aims to establish digital wallets that would allow businesses to securely store and manage their identity and financial information. The wallets would seek to make it easier for companies to conduct transactions and access services across Europe.
posts.whatsNext: Trilogue talks with the Council can begin once the Council side has its own mandate. Closed-door rounds follow; timing is not published.

posts.title: Suspending the application of the rules on extended producer responsibility for waste, waste electrical and electronical equipment and single use plastic waste (Omnibus VIII on environmental legislation)
posts.label: 🗳️ Lead committee adopted its report
posts.summary: This proposal would temporarily pause certain rules requiring producers to manage the waste from their products, including electrical equipment and single-use plastics. The suspension would affect environmental regulations governing how manufacturers handle responsibility for their products' end-of-life disposal.
posts.whatsNext: A negotiating mandate for talks with the Council would usually follow, or the report goes straight to a plenary vote. No deadline applies.

posts.title: Suspending the application of the rules on extended producer responsibility for batteries and waste batteries and packaging and packaging waste (Omnibus VIII on environmental legislation)
posts.label: 🗳️ Lead committee adopted its report
posts.summary: This proposal would temporarily pause rules that require manufacturers to take responsibility for managing batteries and packaging waste at the end of their product's life. The suspension aims to provide relief from these environmental compliance requirements.
posts.whatsNext: A negotiating mandate for talks with the Council would usually follow, or the report goes straight to a plenary vote. No deadline applies.

posts.title: Area of Application of the Southern Indian Ocean Fisheries Agreement (SIOFA): management, conservation and control measures
posts.label: 📋 New legislative proposal
posts.summary: This proposal aims to establish rules for managing fish stocks and monitoring fishing activities in the Southern Indian Ocean to ensure sustainable use of marine resources in that region. It would set out conservation measures and control procedures that fishing vessels and operators would need to follow when operating in these international waters.
posts.whatsNext: Parliament's lead committee and the Council's working party examine it in parallel. No deadline applies at this stage; most files take one to two-plus years.

posts.title: Air passenger rights
posts.label: 📜 Published in the Official Journal
posts.summary: This law establishes protections and compensation rights for airline passengers, including provisions for assistance during delays and cancellations. It requires airlines to inform passengers of their rights and provide care such as meals and accommodation when necessary. Passengers can claim compensation from airlines for significant delays or cancellations under certain circumstances.
posts.whatsNext: It's law. It enters into force on the date it specifies or, if none, the 20th day after publication in the Official Journal.

posts.title: European Union Critical Communication System
posts.label: 📋 New legislative proposal
posts.summary: This proposal seeks to establish a new system that would help coordinate critical communications across the European Union during emergencies or crises. The system would aim to ensure that important alert and warning information can be effectively shared and distributed to the public when needed.
posts.whatsNext: Parliament's lead committee and the Council's working party examine it in parallel. No deadline applies at this stage; most files take one to two-plus years.

posts.title: Use of the European Union Critical Communication System by civil protection services and organisations
posts.label: 📋 New legislative proposal
posts.summary: This proposal aims to establish rules for how member states and civil protection organisations would use a European critical communications system. It seeks to enable these organisations to coordinate and communicate effectively during emergencies and crises.
posts.whatsNext: Parliament's lead committee and the Council's working party examine it in parallel. No deadline applies at this stage; most files take one to two-plus years.

posts.title: Non-road mobile machinery engines: inclusion of hydrogen as a reference fuel for the testing of an engine type or engine family
posts.label: 📋 New legislative proposal
posts.summary: This proposal would modify existing rules for testing engines to allow hydrogen to be used as an alternative fuel option during these tests. The change aims to help evaluate how engines perform when running on hydrogen fuel.
posts.whatsNext: Parliament's lead committee and the Council's working party examine it in parallel. No deadline applies at this stage; most files take one to two-plus years.

posts.title: Union Civil Protection Mechanism and Union support for health emergency preparedness and response
posts.label: 🗳️ Lead committee adopted its report
posts.summary: This proposal aims to strengthen how the EU responds to civil protection emergencies and health crises by improving coordination and support among member states. It seeks to enhance preparedness and response capabilities so that countries can better handle large-scale disasters and health emergencies together.
posts.whatsNext: A negotiating mandate for talks with the Council would usually follow, or the report goes straight to a plenary vote. No deadline applies.

posts.title: Pericles V exchange, assistance and training programme for the protection of the euro against counterfeiting 2028–2034
posts.label: 🗳️ Lead committee adopted its report
posts.summary: The proposal aims to fund a programme that would provide training and support to law enforcement and other officials across participating countries to help them detect and prevent counterfeit euro banknotes and coins. It seeks to strengthen cooperation and share expertise on protecting the currency from counterfeiting threats.
posts.whatsNext: A negotiating mandate for talks with the Council would usually follow, or the report goes straight to a plenary vote. No deadline applies.
